description: Είμαστε μια ομάδα φοιτητών με πάθος για τη διαστημική τεχνολογία και την καινοτομία. Στο φετινό NASA Hackathon, δουλεύουμε πάνω σε μια έξυπνη λύση ψηφιακής υγείας, αξιοποιώντας σύγχρονα δεδομένα και τεχνολογία για να κάνουμε τις μακροχρόνιες αποστολές στο διάστημα πιο ασφαλείς.
summary:
SolarGuard is our NASA Space Apps 2026 project. It protects people from sun and radiation risk by combining smartwatch vitals, NASA POWER solar data,bit flip detections and an AI health assistant. The code is a desktop dashboard (UserInt.py), a scoring engine (healthMonitor.py), a watch reader (smartwatch.py), a radiation test, and a FastAPI chat web app deployed on Render.

Our approach is a clean pipeline. A user uploads a watch export (Apple Health, JSON or CSV), and smartwatch.py parses and normalises it first. The cleaned vitals then flow into UserInt.py and healthMonitor.py, which score them and log each measurement to health_log.csv. Missing metrics fall back to simulated values, and the UI shows which are real. Files load in a background thread, errors are readable, and an Analyze (demo) button replays the latest logged measurement.
details: SolarGuard is a sun-safety monitor that turns smartwatch data into clear health insights. Users upload a watch export (Apple Health, JSON or CSV), and our engine scores their vitals, combines them with NASA POWER solar data and a radiation test, and an AI chatbot explains the results in plain language. It gives people early, understandable warnings without special hardware, aiming to make health monitoring more accessible. We built it in Python with PySide6 for the desktop dashboard, FastAPI on Render for the web app, and the Groq API for the chatbot. It’s creative because it links wearable vitals, space weather and radiation testing in one tool.
